headline: Medium risk overall: shared-output and workflow assumptions create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways, while compliance risk is limited by sparse data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts and REST/gRPC outputs that another agent may consume, while awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list that could ingest those outputs as content. No shared channel is documented, but the pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-produced files or messages as trusted content
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace, queue, or copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Separate the agents into isolated workspaces
Require provenance labels on all agent_a outputs
Strip instructions from any content passed to agent_b
Use a human review step before agent_b consumes agent_a output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress; agent_b has no declared data classes and network egress is none. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or sensitive data class, so leakage is possible only through unusual integration and the blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts contain sensitive data and are copied into agent_b inputs
IF a shared workspace exposes files from agent_a to agent_b
mitigations: Keep sensitive artifacts out of shared folders
Disable automatic file handoff between agents
Redact parameters before passing outputs onward
Review allowlisted egress destinations for agent_a

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows has API-facing workflow execution, but awesome-selfhosted is a static catalog with no write or network capabilities shown. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared write scopes, so direct capability conflict is unlikely and limited if introduced by external orchestration.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF agent_b is extended beyond its documented read-only catalog role
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared writable directories
Lock any shared git or database resources
Keep agent_b read-only

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can produce workflow outputs that agent_b may treat as authoritative catalog content or recommendations. Because agent_b has no documented verification or critique mechanism, the pair can propagate errors from agent_a into downstream knowledge products, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF agent_b republishes or operationalizes agent_a output without verification
IF agent_a output is used as a source of truth for downstream entries
mitigations: Add a verification checklist before reuse
Require source citations for every imported claim
Have a human approve any derived catalog entry
Compare agent_a output against independent references

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no declared PHI, residency, or retention obligations. Compliance risk is therefore mostly about policy mismatch if the operator routes regulated data through agent_a; agent_b has no data classes or egress, so it is not the primary compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_a workflows
IF operator policies require residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
Document retention and deletion rules
Restrict agent_a inputs to non-sensitive artifacts
Review deployment region and logging settings
